IdeaToApps: how the screens look and how a visitor uses them

A walk through the site as a visitor and buyer would see it, in the order they use it. Screenshots were taken from the local test build on 2026-11-15, at desktop width (1440 px) and phone width.

Read this first.
  • These are screenshots of the local test site, not the live site. It is not deployed yet.
  • The ClipForge image is a plain blue placeholder, and the version notes (“Example second release (sandbox data)”) are test data. On the real site you upload the app image and write real release notes.
  • Screens I have not captured: sign in, cart, checkout (Stripe), order confirmation and the WordPress admin screens. Checkout and the admin look are WooCommerce and WordPress defaults styled by the theme. I can capture them if you want.
  • The Privacy, Terms and Refund pages are drafts and carry a DRAFT banner until real legal text is supplied.

The visitor journey in one line

Home → Apps → ClipForge page → Buy (one-time, Stripe checkout) → Sign in → My account → My library → Download any version.

1. Land on the home page

The visitor sees the promise (“Useful apps. Brilliant ideas. One place.”), the featured app card for ClipForge with its price, a four-step “How it works” strip (Discover, Watch, Buy once, Download and run), a newsletter sign-up and the footer links. The moon button in the header switches between dark and light mode. Explore apps leads to the catalog.

2. Browse the apps catalog

Search box, sort menu and one card per app. Today there is one app. Clicking a card opens that app’s page.

3. Read the app page and decide to buy

The app page shows the tagline, the Buy button with the price, what you get, the requirements (Chromium-based desktop browser) and a version list with change notes. The price on the button comes from the linked WooCommerce product. Buy ClipForge adds it to the cart and goes to checkout.

4. After buying: the library

After payment the buyer signs in to My account → My library. Every version is listed, newest first, each with its own Download button. When a new version is added later, past buyers see it here automatically.

Light mode

Every page also has a light theme. The visitor’s choice follows their device setting and the header toggle.
